skill.name: conversation-memory
skill.description: Design persistent conversation memory systems for LLM apps, including short-term memory, long-term memory, entity memory, retrieval, consolidation, and safety boundaries.
skill.summary: Guides LLM memory architecture with tiered storage, entity tracking, retrieval, and user isolation.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported one external command pattern, but the evidence is inline Markdown naming related skills. I found no executable code, shell instructions, network access, data exfiltration, or prompt injection attempts.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 61 uses Markdown inline backticks to list related skill names. It is not Ruby backtick execution, a shell command, or an instruction to execute external commands.

content.value_statement: LLM apps often lose useful context or retrieve irrelevant history. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to design safer memory tiers, retrieval, and isolation.
actual_capabilities: Explains short-term, long-term, and entity memory as separate design tiers.
Lists persistence, retrieval, and consolidation capabilities for assistant memory systems.
Describes memory-aware prompting that includes relevant memories in prompts.
Calls out sharp edges such as unbounded stores, irrelevant retrieval, and user isolation failures.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not include executable memory storage code.
It does not choose a database, embedding model, or vector index.
It does not define privacy policy, retention periods, or compliance controls.
It depends on the user to implement testing and access controls.

use_cases.title: Design a chatbot memory model
use_cases.description: Plan which facts belong in short-term, long-term, and entity memory before implementation.

use_cases.title: Plan entity memory for support
use_cases.description: Define how customer, account, and product facts should be stored, updated, and retrieved.

use_cases.title: Review memory safety risks
use_cases.description: Check a memory design for unbounded growth, irrelevant retrieval, and cross-user leakage.

prompt_templates.title: Map memory tiers
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new assistant.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use conversation-memory to outline short-term, long-term, and entity memory for a personal assistant. Include what each tier stores.

prompt_templates.title: Design retrieval rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for relevance and context control.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use conversation-memory to design retrieval rules for a support chatbot. Include relevance checks, recency rules, and context limits.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an existing memory plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing architecture.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use conversation-memory to review this memory architecture and suggest improvements for persistence, consolidation, retrieval, and prompt inclusion.

prompt_templates.title: Audit isolation controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Use conversation-memory to audit a multi-user assistant memory design for cross-user leakage, stale facts, and missing lifecycle controls.

output_examples.input: Create a memory plan for a customer support assistant.
output: Short-term memory keeps the active ticket and recent messages.
Long-term memory stores stable customer preferences and recurring issues.
Entity memory tracks accounts, products, subscriptions, and support contacts.

output_examples.input: Review this memory design for risks.
output: The main risk is cross-user memory leakage during retrieval.
Add tenant filters before vector search and before prompt assembly.
Add lifecycle rules for expiry, consolidation, and deletion.

best_practices: Separate short-term, long-term, and entity memory so retrieval rules stay clear.
Expire, merge, or archive memories before stores grow without bounds.
Enforce user isolation before retrieval, summarization, and persistence.
anti_patterns: Saving every conversation turn without lifecycle management.
Using one memory store for all memory types and users.
Injecting all stored memories into prompts without relevance checks.

faq.question: Does this skill store data itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance and prompts. Storage must be implemented outside the skill.

faq.question: Can it help choose memory tiers?
faq.answer: Yes. It separates short-term, long-term, and entity memory by purpose and retrieval behavior.

faq.question: Does it include implementation code?
faq.answer: No. It describes patterns and risks, but it does not ship scripts or runtime code.

faq.question: How should sensitive memories be handled?
faq.answer: Use consent, retention limits, access controls, and deletion flows before storing sensitive user information.

faq.question: Can it work with RAG systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It pairs well with retrieval systems when memory relevance and user isolation are enforced.

faq.question: What should be tested first?
faq.answer: Test relevance, stale memory handling, tenant isolation, and behavior when no useful memory exists.
